locator: I q.2 a.3 co., prima via: quia moventia secunda non movent nisi per hoc quod sunt mota a primo movente
interpretation: The explicit per se (essentially ordered) premise. Moventia secunda are read as moved movers whose moving depends here and now on their being moved, as in the instrumental stick and hand example. The formal statement covers every distinct mover that is moved in any respect; it is therefore the strongest premise of the reconstruction and the natural target of objections (for example a mover moved in an irrelevant respect). A per accidens series, such as a father who begets and was himself begotten, is not a MovesAsMoved series on this reading; Aquinas admits that such series could be infinite (ST I q.46 a.2 ad 7, not yet in the corpus).
